steps.claim: §3.4 requires sequential small-step execution and says "every executed instruction pushes a run-history frame". §4.1 store writes N/8 little-endian bytes; §7.4 retains its address, width and overwritten bytes. For a live byte initially 1, store.i8 p 2 followed by load.i8 p and zero-extension must return 2 if execution completes without an ISA fault. A host-storage error is not an instruction that may silently advance past this store with neither its write nor its frame.

At 128 MiB, after request/reply and v are complete, retain before=m.snapshot(). There are four history frames and byte 1 is 1. step_once on the store returns ErrorKind::HostResource citing §7.1/§7.4/§10 sparse memory retention. But before != m.snapshot(): the activation ip changes from 4 to 5; the byte is still 1 and history still has four frames. This is an ordinary Err from the library, not an allocator abort or malformed input.

step increments ip before executing the row. save_bytes records the old byte; Memory::store then attempts fallible sparse copy-on-write/growth. On error, step calls undo_record(undo)? before returning the original error. The new undo_record starts by preparing sparse capacity again whenever undo.bytes is nonempty, even though no store byte changed. That reservation also fails, so it exits before assigning undo.control. At 1 MiB the shared copy can fit but geometric growth cannot; 1.25/1.5 MiB controls also reproduce the failure when the shared copy itself is denied.

Drop the held observer and call step_once again: the next op is load.i8, not the rejected store.i8. run completes with Int(64,1), byte [1], fault=None. At 256 MiB the same program/probe executes the store, adds its frame and returns Int(64,2), byte [2], fault=None. Both children exit 0 and whole-run reversal subsequently restores entry. Thus successful reversal later does not detect the skipped forward operation.

S0 core: fallible shared-memory preparation has introduced a failed rollback that consumes an unexecuted store and permits a wrong successful continuation. This fits no stated INV-1..INV-6 theorem: INV-6 concerns checker labels/resources, not CC store rollback; ISA T4 assumes a valid retained trace and does not justify skipping a forward instruction. The two original R22 blockers can be resolved while this new defect still prevents core and whole-crate acceptance.

blocking.fix: Change src/classical.rs::ClassicalMachine::{step,undo_record} and, as needed, src/retained.rs::SparseBytes::prepare / src/oracle.rs::Memory::store. Prepare writes on an unpublished memory value, or retain a restorable pre-write shared owner, and ensure the failure path restores control and data without repeating an allocation that already failed. Do not merely suppress the rollback error or advance past the instruction. In tests/r22_retention.rs add the exact pinned object above in a fresh 128 MiB child: 1 MiB request and nonzero reply both succeed; hold the prefix snapshot; attempt store; on HostResource assert full prefix equality, four frames, no fault and unchanged transcript/byte. Drop the observer and retry: next op must be store.i8, byte becomes 2, completion returns Int(64,2), and reversal restores entry. Permit a successful first store if an improved representation makes it fit, but then require its write/frame/result; add a deterministically denied preparation case so the failure branch remains exercised. Retain 256 MiB success and small-byte controls, and cover the same preparation/rollback interaction for device writes sharing this path. No ISA size cap or spec change is needed.
